artists.biography:
Dropkick Murphys are an American punk rock band formed in Quincy, Massachusetts in 1996. The band was initially signed to independent punk record label Hellcat Records, releasing five albums for the label, and making a name for themselves locally through constant touring and yearly St. Patrick's Day week shows, held in and around Boston. The 2004 single "Tessie" became the band's first and one of their biggest charting singles to date. The band's final Hellcat release, 2005's The Warrior's Code, included "I'm Shipping Up to Boston", which was featured in the Academy Award-winning movie The Departed and went on to become one of the band's biggest singles, one of their best-known songs, and an anthem for Boston sports teams.

In 2007, the band signed with Warner Bros. Records and began releasing music through their own vanity label, Born & Bred. 2007's The Meanest of Times made its debut at No. 20 on the Billboard charts and featured the band's hit single "The State of Massachusetts", while 2011's Going Out in Style was an even bigger success, making its debut at No. 6, giving the band their highest-charting album to date.The band's eighth studio album, Signed and Sealed in Blood was released in 2013 making its debut at No. 9 on the Billboard charts

perplexity.description:
Dropkick Murphys' 2022 album This Machine Still Kills Fascists is a politically charged and musically vibrant addition to the band's discography, blending their signature Celtic punk sound with folk and country influences. Released on September 30, 2022, through Dummy Luck Music, the album features lyrics written by folk legend Woody Guthrie, many of which were previously unrecorded. The band sets these words to original music, resulting in a collection of ten tracks that merge traditional folk storytelling with the energetic, anthemic style Dropkick Murphys are known for.

Musically, the album stands out for its fusion of acoustic instrumentation, driving rhythms, and socially conscious lyrics, reflecting both Guthrie's legacy and the band's own activist spirit. It marks a unique chapter in Dropkick Murphys' career, as it is their first album to be entirely based on Guthrie's words, highlighting their commitment to folk-punk traditions and political engagement. The album received positive critical attention for its authenticity, lyrical depth, and energetic performances, with reviewers praising its ability to bridge past and present struggles through music.
